items.source_name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories — Lipid Panel, Serum
items.locator: Mayo Clinic Laboratories Test 616696, Lipid Panel, Serum — Patient Preparation/Profile: fasting is specified as 8 hours or more for the cited fasting lipid profile. Medication instructions are not universally replaced by the fasting requirement and should follow the ordering/laboratory instructions.
items.version: Current Mayo Clinic Laboratories test catalog entry 616696; preparation requirement live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.stem: A client is scheduled for a serum lipid panel whose laboratory profile specifies “Fasting (8 HR or more).” Which instruction is most accurate?

options.A: Eat a light meal two hours before collection because fasting does not affect the requested laboratory profile.
options.B: Follow the laboratory requirement and complete at least eight hours of fasting before the specimen is collected.
options.C: Fast for only one hour because longer fasting can invalidate the lipid measurements in this laboratory profile.
options.D: Automatically stop every prescribed morning medicine because all fasting lipid panels require withholding all medications.

items.rationale: The cited Mayo Clinic Laboratories lipid-panel profile specifies fasting for 8 hours or more. Option B directly follows the laboratory's preparation requirement. Option A ignores the ordered fasting condition, Option C shortens it below the specified interval, and Option D incorrectly turns fasting into a universal instruction to stop prescribed medications; medication directions must follow individualized orders or laboratory instructions.

items.locator: CDC — Safer Food Choices for People With Weakened Immune Systems: choose pasteurized products and thoroughly cooked meat/eggs, wash produce, avoid raw sprouts and other higher-risk foods, and heat deli meats/hot dogs until steaming hot or 165°F when recommended for people with weakened immune systems.
items.version: Current CDC food-safety guidance for people with weakened immune systems; live federal source rechecked 2026-08-15. Blueprint corrected from Basic Care and Comfort to Safety & Infection Prevention and Control because the tested objective is prevention of foodborne infection in a highly susceptible client.

items.locator: NCBI Bookshelf/Open RN Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd ed. (2024), Communication strategies for hearing impairment: face the client directly in good lighting, facilitate visual access, speak clearly without shouting/exaggeration, minimize background noise, and use the client's preferred written/assistive communication methods as needed.
items.version: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd edition (2024), current NCBI Bookshelf resource rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: NCBI Bookshelf/Open RN Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd ed. (2024), Communication strategies for visual impairment: identify yourself when approaching/entering, provide adequate lighting when useful, read pertinent information aloud, verbally orient the client and describe locations of important objects rather than relying on gestures or companions.
items.version: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd edition (2024), current NCBI Bookshelf resource rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: Cochrane Review CD009199 — Body position and intake of fluids for preventing headache after a lumbar puncture: routine bed rest after lumbar puncture does not prevent post-dural-puncture headache and may increase its occurrence; extra fluid intake has not shown preventive benefit. Routine prolonged flat positioning solely for prevention is not supported.
items.version: Cochrane systematic review published 2016-03-07 remains the active evidence review at the cited source; currentness and absence of a superseding Cochrane conclusion rechecked 2026-08-15. Blueprint corrected to Reduction of Risk Potential because the item tests prevention of a complication after a diagnostic procedure, explicitly represented in the 2026 NCSBN test plan.

items.locator: CDC — Adult Immunization Schedule by Age, current schedule: vaccination in older adults is based on age, prior doses/history and risk factors; the ≥65-year age rows/notes include indicated recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccination along with other age/risk-based vaccines.
items.version: Current CDC adult schedule is the July 2, 2025 schedule as amended 2026-04-27 under the March 16, 2026 court order; current CDC schedule status live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.rationale: Older adulthood does not end routine vaccination. The current CDC adult schedule requires review of age, prior vaccination history, and risk factors; recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccines are among the vaccines routinely considered in this age range, along with other indicated vaccines. Option D appropriately directs history-based use of the current schedule. Options A, B, and C incorrectly exclude age-indicated vaccination or impose unsupported prerequisites.

items.locator: ACOG — Exercise During Pregnancy: in uncomplicated pregnancy without medical/obstetric contraindications, physical activity is safe and desirable; pregnant individuals should generally obtain at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week, with activity individualized and adjusted for symptoms/clinical changes.
items.version: Current ACOG Exercise During Pregnancy patient/professional guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: AHRQ Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit, Tool 16 — Help Patients Take Medicine Correctly: identify adherence barriers; simplify medication schedules when possible; link doses with daily routines; use pill organizers, charts, family supports, alarms or electronic reminders as appropriate to the individual's barriers.
items.version: AHRQ Tool 16 last reviewed 2024-04 and remains current on the federal AHRQ site; live source rechecked 2026-08-15.

items.locator: NIMH — Eating Disorders: What You Need to Know, Anorexia Nervosa: severe restriction of food intake, intense fear of gaining weight/behaviors interfering with weight gain, significantly low body weight/extreme thinness, distorted body image and lack of recognition/denial of the seriousness of low weight are characteristic features.
items.version: Current NIMH eating-disorders publication live-rechecked 2026-08-15; difficulty corrected to easy because the item is direct syndrome recognition with clearly differentiated eating-disorder distractors.

items.locator: CDC — Treatment and Intervention for Autism Spectrum Disorder, developmental/educational supports: many autistic people benefit from consistency, routines that can be written or drawn, pairing verbal instructions with visual supports, and Social Stories that provide simple descriptions of what to expect in a situation.
items.version: Current CDC autism treatment/intervention guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
